thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - eu-west-1 runtime cluster experiencing autoscaler surge + node flaps. Multiple inference pods restarting with CUDA OOMs and driver resets. Root TS: 2310007777
sre_kamal: grabbing this. Seeing a spike of CrashLoopBackOff on inference-prod-7x and inference-prod-9b. Quick paste from pod log:
```
2026-03-16T05:12:03Z inference-prod-9b RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.80 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 28.92 GiB already allocated)
  File "/app/serve/loader.py", line 198, in load_model
```
eng-runtime: looks like concurrent cold start allocations during scale bursts. Memory pressure + driver resets (nvidia) cause pods to OOM and then nodes to report GPU kernel reset.
eng-platform: recall we flipped on fast-burst autoscaling for a new tenant group in eu-west-1 in the last deploy (rollout 2310006000). CA is permitting very aggressive launch rates.
oncall_zoe: paging PD and tagging folks: @eng-runtime @eng-platform @ops_rafa @sre_kamal. Are we seeing any customer-impact metrics?
cs_clara: CS reports intermittent 503s for embedding and batch endpoints. Affected customers concentrated in EU. No data corruption reported, but higher error rate and latency spikes since ~05:10 UTC.
sre_kamal: quick diagnostics: autoscaler events show scale 3 -> 18 -> 4 within ~3 minutes. HPA/CA stabilization 0s. Node events show Kubelet OOM messages and GPU driver resets. I'm concerned about simultaneous cold starts for ~15 pods.
eng-runtime: model variant "embed-large-quant" uses mmap-backed tensors and tries to preallocate working set on startup. When many pods cold-start concurrently, aggregate GPU memory pressure spikes. Also saw a bad driver reset pattern in kernel logs.
ops_rafa: dmesg on node g4-eu-21: multiple "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" and driver reloads. Kernel shows GPU reset at 05:11:38.
eng-platform: immediate mitigation proposal:
1) disable CA burst for eu-west-1 (stop creating many nodes at once)
2) set HPA stabilization windows to 300s and set a conservative minReplicas (6) for runtime namespace
3) pin traffic to stable model variant with lower cold-start memory (embed-large-quant-safe)
4) cordon and drain flappy nodes and replace drivers where needed
5) flip a runtime env var to avoid eager preloading: SERVE_EAGER_LOAD=false for new pods
oncall_zoe: agree. Execute mitigations now and keep me updated. I'll take primary coordination and own customer comms until handoff.
eng-platform: applying CA burst disable (annotating CA):
```
kubectl -n kube-system annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler autoscaler.k8s.io/disable-burst=true --overwrite
```
eng-platform: patching HPA and minReplicas:
```
kubectl -n runtime patch hpa runtime-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6,"behavior":{"scaleUp":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":300},"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":300}}}}'
```
sre_kamal: HPA patched, minReplicas=6, stabilization windows set. CA annotation applied. CA config picks it up in ~40s.
ops_rafa: cordoning g4-eu-21 and draining now: `kubectl cordon g4-eu-21 && kubectl drain g4-eu-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`
eng-runtime: reweighted route: 90% to embed-large-quant-safe, 10% to canary. Also bumped graceful startup delay to reduce parallel allocations.
eng-runtime: pushed SERVE_EAGER_LOAD=false to deployment and restarted pods progressively to avoid synchronized cold starts.
sre_kamal: metric snapshot pre/post: before mitigations error rate for embeddings ~12% and OOM events ~22/min. After HPA/CA changes and reweighting, error rate down to ~2% and OOM events ~1/min within 8 minutes. CrashLoopBackOff count reduced by ~60%.
cs_clara: notifying impacted customers: sent an interim note explaining mitigation and that we're investigating RCA. Offering prioritized support if they want a dedicated warm pool.
oncall_zoe: handoff checklist for follow-up:
- RCA: driver resets vs memory pressure interplay.
- Long-term: implement autoscale damping/cooldown and per-pool warm replicas, model cold-start memory profiles, GPU health probe and alerting.
- Runbook updates: add steps for disabling CA burst and safe reweighting.
ops_rafa: replacing two nodes with observed resets; provisioning nodes with updated NVIDIA driver (vendor patch) and will roll across pool. Filing INFRA-4902 for driver rollout.
eng-platform: recommendation for permanent change: add per-pool autoscale cooldown config and prefer warm pool approach (keep N warm replicas per pool), and add HPA behavior defaults (stabilization > 180s) in runtime clusters.
eng-runtime: will instrument model load to avoid eager full-GPU allocations during init; schedule synthetic load test tomorrow 09:00 UTC to validate. Also adding telemetry for per-model cold-start alloc peaks.
incident-bot: note added to timeline. Assigning incident owner to oncall_zoe for postmortem. :page_with_curl:
oncall_zoe: summary for ops handoff to night: mitigations applied (CA burst disabled, HPA stabilization to 300s, minReplicas 6, cordon/drain of flappy nodes, pinned traffic to safer model variant, disabled eager load). Customer impact: intermittent 4-14% request errors in EU for ~20 minutes (root cause autoscale thrash causing concurrent cold starts, GPU OOMs and driver resets). Next actions: RCA, driver rollout, autoscale damping, runbook update.
ops_rafa: taking handoff for node replacement and driver rollout. I'll monitor GPU reset metrics and file infra tickets. :white_check_mark:
sre_kamal: leaving monitoring on this but handing active ownership to ops_rafa and eng-runtime for remediation.
eng-runtime: scheduling internal follow-up and will attach load-test results to the postmortem.
cs_clara: follow-up email sent to customers with timeline and mitigation summary.
incident-bot: incident acknowledged -> monitored. Closing active pager loop and moving to postmortem tracking. Thread end.
